objectified_fact_types.fact_type: Student enrolls in Offering with Grade
objectified_fact_types.description: The enrollment relationship is itself treated as an entity, with its own identity and the associated grade as a property. This allows enrollments to be tracked, queried, and referenced independently.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings... At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: Identification of Enrollment entity is not specified. If 'Student enrolls in Offering with Grade' is objectified as an Enrollment entity, what is the reference mode for Enrollment? Is it auto-generated, derived from the Student+Offering combination, or explicitly assigned?

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings... At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: Optionality of grade in enrollment is unclear. The transcript states 'a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in' (line 31), but does not clarify whether every enrollment must have a grade assigned, or if a student can be enrolled without a grade (e.g., still taking the course, or withdrew without a final grade). Is the Grade role mandatory?

source_references.excerpt: What about grades?... At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: Cardinality of enrollment is not fully specified. While 'a student gets at most one grade per offering' (line 31) establishes uniqueness on the Student-Offering combination, it does not explicitly state whether a student must be enrolled in at least one offering (mandatory participation on Student side) or whether every offering must have at least one enrolled student (mandatory participation on Offering side).

source_references.excerpt: A student gets at most one grade per offering.

ambiguities.description: Course title uniqueness is not stated. Can two different courses share the same title, or is CourseTitle also a candidate key? The transcript implies CourseCode is the primary identifier, but does not rule out title duplicates.

source_references.excerpt: Every course has a title and a credit value.

ambiguities.description: Semester date constraints are not specified. Do the start date and end date have any relationship (e.g., must start_date < end_date)? Are there any constraints on overlapping semesters?

source_references.excerpt: A semester has a start date and an end date.

ambiguities.description: Credit value constraints are stated informally. The transcript says credit values are 'usually between 1 and 6' (line 19), but does not specify whether this is a hard constraint or merely a typical range. Should the value constraint on CreditValue include these bounds, or is it unrestricted?

source_references.excerpt: The credit value is a whole number, usually between 1 and 6.

ambiguities.description: Temporal aspects of enrollment are not addressed. When a student receives a grade, is this recorded at enrollment time, or retroactively at the end of the semester? Should the model capture enrollment dates (e.g., date enrolled, date grade assigned)?

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: Cardinality of instructor teaching is not fully specified. While the transcript states 'each offering is taught by exactly one instructor' (line 11) and 'an instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester' (line 11), it does not clarify whether an instructor must teach at least one offering, or can be idle.

source_references.excerpt: Each offering is taught by exactly one instructor. An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester.
